description: Cut the per-call CholeskyQR2 + orthogonality-gate overhead shared across the low-rank peel calls on shape 6 (brief-73: ~47ms of CQR2 trsm/potrf/syrk + gate GEMMs + gather/scatter spread across the dense-LR, psd-LR, and rest-cluster calls). The mixed512 peel currently makes SEPARATE _eigh_lowrank_safe calls per subset (dense k352, psd k256), each paying its own CQR2 + gate + gather. Fuse the dense and psd low-rank subset solves into ONE batched low-rank call (shared Gram/CQR2/gate over the combined subset, split k handled by padding to max-k or a bucketed batched solve), collapsing 2 sets of CQR2/gate GEMMs into 1. Also fold the per-subset residual-gate A@Q recompute into a single batched gate. Per-matrix gated; pure torch.

Fuse mixed512 dense(k352)+psd(k256) low-rank subsets into ONE _eigh_lowrank_safe_multi call: bucketed cores (each subset's k-dependent CQR2 + reduced-eigh megakernel kept separate = compute-identical to parent's 2 calls) but FUSED gate/sync/gather/scatter over the union. Refactored the gate into shared _lr_gate_and_fallback; _eigh_lowrank_safe now a thin wrapper. geomean 28565us (parent 28569, NOISE), shape6 107.20ms (parent 107.26), shape3 78.00ms unaffected. 39/39 validate. Profile: gate V^TV tf32gemm 45->43 (-2), gather 4->3 (2 subset gathers->1), BUT CatArray 8->12 (bucket V/lam/Res cat offsets it) -> net neutral. CQR2 batch_trsm 58->58 + reduced-eigh 2->2 unchanged (k-dependent, correctly NOT fused). stream absent.

MEASURED the brief's PADDING variant: dense+psd fused into ONE _lowrank_eigh at max-k=352 (psd padded up). shape6 107.2ms->143.4ms (+36ms +34%), geomean 28565->29208 (+2.2% REGRESSION). Cause (confirmed): psd at k=352 blows its ~300 inner-solve orth ceiling (PSD probe table: k=352->orth 4.6) so ~256 psd mats mass-fall-back to per-matrix cuSOLVER syevd (~0.85ms each). PADDING WASTE (256 mats x ~32.6us extra reduced-eigh at kk=352 + full cuSOLVER fallback) >> the ~microsecond launch saving. 39/39 validate (gate+fallback keeps correctness). Padding is a decisive measured LOSS -- bucketing is required.

KEEPER: bucketed fusion (FUSE_MODE=bucketed) restored. Re-measured geomean 28534us (parent 28569, t0 28565 -- all NOISE), shape6 107.28ms, shape3 78.00ms. 5-seed reseed sweep (seeds 770001/111111/424242/990099/222222): shape6 39/39 PASS lr_fallback_post=0 (fallback_pre 0-5 all NS-rescued, == parent), shape3 39/39 PASS lr_fallback_post=0 (thin-wrapper refactor preserved shape3's whole-batch route). Op-counts vs parent: gate tf32gemm 45->43, gather 4->3, trsm 58->58, reduced-eigh 2->2. stream absent (grep -ci = 0).

Remove n*n Res concatenation from the fused path: eigen-residual ratio ||Res||_1/||a||_1 computed PER BUCKET (per-matrix norm independent -> bit-identical) then cat only the scalar, so Res never crosses buckets. geomean 28551us (t2 28534, parent 28569 -- all NOISE), shape6 107.31ms, shape3 78.06ms. 5-seed reseed shape6 39/39 lr_fallback_post=0, shape3 39/39 lr_fallback_post=0 (== parent/t2). CatArray still 12 (Vs/lams cat dominate; Res removal offset by per-bucket norm temporaries) so measurement-equivalent to t2 -- a clean simplification, not a further speedup. stream absent.

RESULT: fusing the genuinely-shareable per-call overhead is MEASURED NEUTRAL (geomean 28551us vs parent 28569, shape6 107.31ms vs 107.26 -- all sub-1% noise), non-regressing, safe; PADDING to fuse the differently-k'd cores is a MEASURED LOSS.

WHAT I BUILT (keeper t2/t3): refactored the residual+orth gate + NS-rescue + cuSOLVER-fallback into a shared _lr_gate_and_fallback; _eigh_lowrank_safe is now a thin wrapper; added _eigh_lowrank_safe_multi(a, buckets) that solves dense (k352) and psd (k256) at their OWN k (k-dependent CQR2 + reduced-eigh megakernel kept bucketed = compute-identical to parent's 2 calls) while FUSING everything k-independent: ONE combined gate over the union, ONE bad.any() device->host sync (brief-67-safe, no new .item()), ONE NS-rescue + ONE cuSOLVER fallback, ONE gather of af, ONE scatter. t3 further removed the n*n Res concat (per-bucket eig ratio).

OP-COUNTS (nsys shape6, parent -> keeper): gate V^TV tf32gemm 45->43 (2 subset gate-GEMM sets -> 1), vectorized_gather 4->3 (2 subset gathers -> 1). But CatArray 8->12 (catting the two buckets' V/lam for the shared scatter). CQR2 batch_trsm_left<float> 58->58 and reduced-eigh mega_eigh_med_split 2->2 UNCHANGED -- correctly NOT fused (k-dependent).

WHY NEUTRAL (the measured lever finding): the fusable overhead is tiny. nsys shape6 breakdown: rest-cluster mega_eigh_clust_split_k = 44.5% (45ms, ONE custom-kernel launch, off-limits), reduced-eigh mega_eigh_med_split = 14.4% (14.6ms, 2 instances: dense-k352 11.48ms + psd-k256 3.16ms), CQR2 batch_trsm = 7.6% (7.7ms). The gate+gather I fused is ~15us total (tf32gemm sum 2.90ms vs parent 2.92ms) and the added V/lam cat offsets it. The brief-73 '~47ms of CQR2+gate' is dominated by the k-dependent CQR2 trsm + reduced-eigh, which are COMPUTE-bound and per-k, not launch-bound shared overhead.

PADDING (t1, brief's named variant, MEASURED): dense+psd fused into ONE _lowrank_eigh at max-k=352 -> geomean 28565->29208 (+2.2%), shape6 107.2ms->143.4ms (+36ms +34%). Cause: psd at k=352 blows its ~300 inner-solve orth ceiling (PSD probe: k352->orth 4.6) so ~256 psd mats mass-fall-back to per-matrix cuSOLVER syevd; plus each psd mat pays 352^2 reduced-eigh (~32.6us) vs its 256^2. PADDING WASTE >> launch saving -- decisive loss, as the brief anticipated. Bucketing is required.

A DIRECT batched megakernel that tiles MIXED block-widths (352 and 256) in one launch WITHOUT padding psd up would fuse the 2 launches with zero padding waste -- but that is an nvcc kernel change (megakernel .cu), out of scope for this pure-torch brief and other workers may be building. (3) The rest-cluster mega_eigh_clust_split_k (45ms, 44.5%) remains the dominant shape6 cost and is the highest-value target overall (off-limits here as a custom kernel). (4) Folding the two-level and rest-cluster paths' OWN gates into a single combined gate over the ENTIRE captured set (dense+psd+twolevel+rest) was not attempted -- those are different gate structures (different algorithms), a larger structural change than this brief scoped.
